correctness.rationale: The quotient graph on 2^(d-1) vertices has no triangles and each two-edge path completes uniquely to a four-cycle for every d>=5. All dual faces are enumerated symbolically by the connected-triple criterion. Two explicit elementary collapses per four-cycle reduce the Alexander dual to the square CW complex with one circle for each vertex pair of distance at least three. The square CW complex is a free antipodal quotient of the simply connected cubical two-skeleton, giving pi1=Z/2. Its f-vector yields H2 free of rank B_d. Universal coefficients and integral Alexander duality yield exactly the claimed two groups with no other homology. The standalone checker independently verifies all small-face and free-face claims for d=5,6, the F_2/F_3/F_5 boundary ranks, exhaustive d=5 dual membership and an acyclic d=5 Morse matching with attaching degrees 0 or ±2. The code is finite corroboration; the infinite proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The formula gives an infinite family of natural distance-regular graphs whose pure ordinary three-cut complexes have unavoidable Z/2 torsion and lower-dimensional nonzero rational homology. It supplies exact closed-form free ranks and a geometric cause via the antipodal covering, in contrast with the constructed torsion examples and torsion-free families in the foundational literature. It is neither a graph renaming nor an arbitrary finite slice: the graph family and cut construction are canonical, and the square-cover mechanism persists for all d>=5.
